Paul — thanks, diagram received and helpful. Answers inline below and a proposed sequencing.

- ASN: Redwood will peer from ASN 65123 (already allocated for private deployments).
- MTU: we will run MTU 9000 on the internal data fabric (intra‑rack and cross‑connect). For the public egress path we will do PMTUD and set TCP MSS clamp at the edge to avoid fragmentation toward internet paths.
- Control plane: control plane management traffic will be on a dedicated VLAN (mgmt VLAN 210) with a separate /24 (10.41.210.0/24) reachable only to NexaCloud NOC and our management bastions. Data plane traffic will use tenant VLANs and overlay interfaces.
- NAT: we prefer to terminate customer egress NAT in the warehouse (Redwood edge) for observability and egress policy enforcement. However, if NexaCloud requires upstream NAT for billing reasons we can align — give us the exact SNAT ranges.
- Ops contact: primary is me (laura.bennett@redwood.com) and backup is jonas.weber@redwood.com. Mobile numbers in the signature.

Proposed cutover cadence (two phases):
1) Control plane prep & verification (window T‑1): establish management BGP session, validate mgmt reachability, confirm cert exchange and mTLS endpoints for control plane API. Smoke tests: ssh to management IPs, curl control API /health, cert check.
2) Data plane attach (window T): bring overlay interfaces, validate KV cache routing, run traffic‑shaping tests, iperf checks across racks. Verify MTU end‑to‑end and sample tokenized inference calls to ensure end‑to‑end connectivity and latency metrics.

I'll upload a short preflight runbook (controlplane_dataplane_matrix.xlsx) with the verification steps and expected evidence. Can NexaCloud accept a staged BGP up (hold timers relaxed) so we can test without impacting production?

Laura Bennett
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Laura / Paul — quick notes from SRE/networking perspective: 

- HA: For the control plane we will bring a dual‑homed HA pair (two control plane nodes in separate PDUs/racks). Peer both to NexaCloud so we can fail a single control plane node without disrupting API calls.
- L2 vs L3 adjacency: prefer L3 peering at the edge (BGP) and L2 only inside our aggregate fabric. Avoid extending customer L2 into our pods.
- KV cache traffic: ensure we advertise more specific routes for the KV cache subnets; this prevents hairpinning across fabric. We'll provide the prefix list during the preflight.
- MTU/PMTUD: if you run jumbo frames, add an iptables MSS clamp at the egress NAT to protect clients reaching smaller MTU hops (we've seen issues with certain carrier links).
- Tests: include UDP iperf for MTU detection, TCP iperf for performance, plus a series of 50 synthetic inference calls to validate end‑to‑end token latency. We'll capture token latency traces in the console.

Can procurement and schedule folks confirm: Do we need a signed PO before we start pre‑staging the cross‑connect or is an MSA sufficient? Marissa?

– Jonas
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference
